what: `on.request.role` lets an HTTP flow run only for a caller who holds the role it names, or one of the roles when it names several. It requires sign-in by itself (`auth: required` need not be written): a signed-out caller gets 401 `{"error":"Unauthorized"}` and a signed-in caller without the role 403 `{"error":"Forbidden"}`, before any step runs and before the inputs are checked. A flow without `role:` has no role gate (public_flows covers `auth:`). Scheduled and data-event flows have no caller and take no `role:`.
several_roles: The value is one role name (`role: finance`), a comma-separated list (`role: "warehouse, manager"`) or a YAML list (`role: [warehouse, manager]`, yaml_example). A list is any-of: a caller who holds one of the names passes. Spaces around a name are dropped. A space inside one is part of the name: `role: warehouse manager` is ONE role name, and gets a warning. A value that names no role or holds an empty name (`role: []`, `role: "warehouse,"`, `role: "warehouse,,manager"`) and a YAML map are refused when the file is written.
matching: Each name is compared exactly (letter case included) with every role the caller holds: the account's own role (`_benmore_users.role`), its unexpired role grants (global ones, and those for the caller's current tenant) and its tenant membership role (groups.role_field) in the current tenant. A flow gate has no role order: `role: editor` does not admit a `manager`. A global admin passes every role gate, so `role: finance` means finance or a global admin. `admin` (any letter case), alone or in a list, is not matched by name: only a global admin passes by it, never a tenant membership role or tenant-scoped grant named admin, so `role: [admin, finance]` admits a global admin and a finance member and not a tenant admin. api({at:'rbac'}) gotchas says which accounts are global admins.
warnings: A write of the file, `benmore check` and the app's log when it loads the file give a warning for a gate that is accepted and probably not meant. A name that the app names nowhere, when app.yaml has a `roles:` block: not under roles:, not groups.bootstrap.founding_role or the default of the membership role column, not in an access `role:` or `owner_or_role:` mode or a workflow transition (`admin` and `user` are built in). It is usually a typo, which nobody holds; a tenant role that exists only as data in the membership table is warned about too and can be ignored. A name with a space in it. And `admin` in an app whose tenant members can hold a role named admin (groups.role_field with groups.bootstrap.founding_role: admin, a membership role column that defaults to admin, or `admin` declared under roles:): tenant admins do not pass by that name. A deployed file whose value holds an empty role name still loads, admits only a global admin and logs the warning.
tenant_admins: When a tenant's own admins should call the flow, write `auth: required` and refuse in the first step from the caller's membership row: a SQL step with id `me`, `SELECT id FROM <groups.table> WHERE <groups.key> = :org AND <groups.user_field> = :user_id AND <groups.role_field> IN ('admin', 'finance')` with `params: { org: "${{ user.group_id || 0 }}" }`, then `if: ${{ !steps.me.outputs.rows }}` with `run: respond` and `with: { status: 403, json: { error: forbidden } }`. A signed-in caller with no tenant has no `user.group_id`: the `|| 0` makes the query match no row, where a bare reference fails the step with a 500. Or give the tenant role a name of its own (org_admin) and name it in `role:`.
async: `role:` works on a `mode: async` flow, one name or a list: the request is refused with 401 or 403 instead of the 202, and the role is checked again when the job starts (api({at:'async-flows'}) identity). A check written as a step (tenant_admins) cannot refuse the caller there: the 202 is sent before any step runs, and a `respond` step does nothing in the job. Put a synchronous `auth: required` flow in front of the work: it checks the caller, queues the work with `run: enqueue` and answers 202 itself with the enqueue step's `job_id`. Gate the queued flow `role: admin`, so that nobody but a global admin calls it directly (enqueue).
where_it_applies: The gate decides every way the flow runs for a caller: the request, the job of a `mode: async` flow, scheduling it (POST /api/_scheduled answers 403), its line in /_internal/flows.json (a caller without the role does not get the flow, so `bm.flows.<name>` is absent for them) and a connector tool that calls it. A job queued by `run: enqueue` has no caller, so the gate does not apply to it. A scoped credential (an API token or Bearer session with explicit scopes) is covered by permissions.
yaml_example:
# flows/receive-stock.yaml - a role gate that names several roles: a caller
# who holds any of them passes, and so does a global admin.
on:
  request:
    method: POST
    path: /api/receive-stock
    role: [warehouse, manager]
jobs:
  receive:
    steps:
      - run: sql
        with: { query: "INSERT INTO stock_moves (sku, kind, moved_by) VALUES (:sku, 'receive', :user_id)" }
      - run: respond
        with: { status: 201, json: { received: true } }
